issue.title: Add integrity metadata to TypeScript bundles

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
This PR adds integrity checks to TypeScript Dag bundles and verifies them before the Node coordinator starts task execution.

`airflow-ts-pack` produces a directly executable `bundle.mjs` containing:

1. An `airflowBundle` comment with byte ranges and SHA-256 digests.
2. An `airflowMetadata` comment describing the SDK, Dags, and task IDs.
3. The bundled JavaScript.

Both comments contain compact JSON, with no base64 encoding. Metadata and executable bytes have independent digests. `airflow_bundle_metadata_version` versions the bundle contract; the header has no separate version field.

The Python reader handles bounded reads, framing validation, digest verification, and a bounded file-identity cache. The coordinator selects the first usable configured bundle declaring the requested Dag. It skips corrupt or incompatible candidates, includes wrong-Dag candidates in rejection diagnostics, and retains traceback logging. The format is documented in `task-sdk/docs/ts-bundle-spec.rst`.

The digests detect corruption, not authenticity: someone who can replace the bundle can also replace its digests. The documented verify-to-execution race and filesystem cache assumptions remain deployment limitations.

Author-written source embedding is deliberately deferred. The `source` metadata field is a logical filename, not retrievable source content. This follows the narrower integrity-focused direction discussed in [the issue clarification](https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/69905#issuecomment-5174764657), rather than implementing every AFBNDL01 feature. The unreleased metadata-first prototype is not supported.

Validation includes cross-language golden fixtures, malformed framing, metadata/code corruption, cache invalidation, direct Node execution, and ordered multi-bundle selection. A real PostgreSQL/LocalExecutor environment with scheduler and standalone Dag processor exercised the SDK example, overlapping bundles, corruption rejection before any Node launch, fallback, exact restoration, and recovery. Host UI-port forwarding was unavailable in Colima; backend health and execution were verified through the internal API.

After the final rebase, all 166 coordinator tests and 237 TypeScript tests passed, along with TypeScript build/lint/typecheck, focused formatting, Ruff, Task SDK mypy, and spelling checks. The full daemon run used the identical contribution code before the final unrelated base refresh. Independent review checked both the original and rebased diff.

issue.title: TS SDK: minify packed bundles and find them by metadata, not filename

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
- related: #69905
- follow-up to review comments on #72046
- **next**: #73127

## Why

1. `NodeCoordinator` hard coded the `bundle.mjs` when discovery, so a `bundles_root` could hold only one bundle and its name was fixed. That defeats the Dag-to-bundle routing the embedded metadata already supports.
2. The TS SDK artifact is not compiled with minify option, which means we have to deploy multiple *.js rather than having just one .min.js artifact.


## How

- Search each root recursively for `*.min.mjs` and select on metadata like`JavaCoordinator` walks for `*.jar` and `ExecutableCoordinator` walks for executables. One root can now hold several bundles, and each Dag is routed to whichever bundle declares it.
- Minify the esbuild output. A digest over the code region is only worth taking when the artifact is not something
  anyone reads or edits in place, which is what `.min` records.
- `airflow-ts-pack` gains `--outfile`, rejecting it alongside `--outdir` and rejecting a name the coordinator could
  never find.

The bundle container format is unchanged. Minification only changes which bytes land inside the already-digested code region.

issue.title: TS SDK: embed the entrypoint source in the Dag bundle

issue.body:
- related: #69905
- follow-up to review comments on #72046
- **Depends on https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/73126 get merged first** (only the last commit is new here).
- **Diff for early review**: https://github.com/jason810496/airflow/compare/refactor/ts-sdk/bundle-discovery-and-minify...feature/ts-sdk/bundle-entrypoint-source

## Why

The shipped code region is minified, so it was nothing readable for Airflow to display for a natively authored TypeScript Dag so we need another section in the artifact to show the entry point raw source.

## How

- A packed bundle now carries the entry module as its author wrote it, in a region with its own byte range and SHA-256 digest in the layout header:

  ```
  //# airflowBundle={"code":{...},"metadata":{...},"source":{...}}
  //# airflowMetadata={...}
  /*# airflowSource
  <the entrypoint, readable>
  #*/
  <minified code>
  ```

- Only the entry module will be included in the source, not the whole module graph behind it.
- A block comment rather than the line comments the layout and metadata use.
- The source range's length is declared rather than derivable from a newline, so the reader pins it by checking that the prescribed opener and closer sit where the declared range implies.
- Rename the metadata `dags` mapping to `task_handlers`, which is what a TypeScript bundle currently provides: handlers for Dags declared elsewhere, not Dag definitions of its own.
- The cross-language golden fixture is reworked. Its code region was the raw contents of a `.ts` fixture while its
  source region was a trivial `export {};`, which is backwards from what the packer emits.
  - It now carries a code region nobody could read and a source region that exercises both escape branches,
    so the Python reader is validated against bytes the TypeScript encoder actually produced.
  - The fixture is added to `.prettierignore`, which would otherwise reformat it and invalidate its digests.
